doc.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021

title: Should critics be musicians; writing in plain language
summary: Playing is not necessary for a critic, with Whitney Balliett as example, and he favors simple words over insider jargon.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: I recall doing an interview with a wonderful guy, a veteran trombonist. And I happened to bring up something that Gary Giddins wrote. And he immediately said, “Does he play anything? Has he ever played anything?” Like he didn’t even let me finish my sentence, it was like that was the hurdle for him in order to give some kind of credence to what Gary wrote. Had he played something. Do you think that’s important?

Yeah it’s important for a jazz critic to have as much knowledge as possible, and if you play a little bit of music that’s good. But it’s not necessary. I mean Whitney Balliet, the best of all writers on jazz, he was always my favorite. You could read his reviews and you could almost hear the music of the people he’s writing about. And I think he played drums a little bit but he didn’t really play music very often. It’s not necessary at all. I mean if it’s musicians reviewing musicians it’s going to be an obvious conflict of interest eventually because they might be complimenting them because they want to get a gig. Or maybe they’re a friend of theirs and you know it’s not that way. It’s a different profession. I mean writers are not frustrated musicians. Now if you hear some of them playing you might say they’re frustrating musicians, but not frustrated.
I think musicians writing about musicians could tend to also use too much sort of inside language that the average reader might find a little alienating.

Well you know you can’t have an attitude in your writing. I mean there are some writers like I feel like I need a dictionary to figure out what they’re talking about. And that’s not what you’re aiming for. I use small words. I mean my vocabulary is not that large. If I have to know French to try to be able to figure out what they’re saying then they’ve failed.
